admin.description: The record about the record: charter, reviews, decisions.

diary.description: Dated capture — daily notes and weekly reviews.

dossier.description: A pointer page for an identity document, permit, or credential.

folk.description: The people workspace: persons and the animals they keep.

gear.description: A durable owned thing worth tracking.

guild.description: Organisations, and the people met through them.

haunt.description: A place that anchors a period of a life.

kin.description: Immediate family — parents, siblings, the household.

ledger.description: Holdings and the things they buy.

persona.description: Any page standing for a named person.

roaming.description: Places and happenings away from home.

routing.description: A page whose job is routing: a concise overview plus curated links onward.

strand.description: A standing topic — a domain page that owns facts about its subject.

vault.description: Money: accounts, spending, and the institutions behind them.

venture.description: A body of work with an aim and a lifecycle.

wellbeing.description: Standing subjects about the body and its upkeep.

workshop.description: Ventures and the organisations that host them.

phone.description: The phone's own stores: contacts, photos, notes, reminders.

registry.description: An official register or issuing authority.

web.description: A page on the open web, snapshotted before it was cited.

raw.description: An item already captured into this record's archive.

photo.description: A photograph, read for what it shows.

identity.description: Who or what the entity is — full name, birth date, the naming facts.

contact.description: How the entity is reached: phone, handle, email.

address.description: Where something is: a home, a workplace, a shop.

housing.description: Where the entity lives, at the granularity the record keeps.

education.description: Degrees, schools, programmes. Multi-valued in practice; a reclassification candidate once the census says so.

event.description: A dated occurrence; recurring ones belong on the Timeline.

account.description: An account or membership held with an institution.

date.description: A standing date that is not itself an event — a renewal, an anniversary.

language.description: Languages spoken, and at what level.

family.description: Household and kinship facts stated as facts, not as relations.

health.description: Standing health facts. Sensitive by default.

plan.description: A stated intention with a target period.

preference.description: Taste, stated or inferred. Observations accumulate; hedges are kept verbatim.

opinion.description: A stated view. Record the variance; a later contrary view never overwrites an earlier one.

habit.description: Observed behaviour, described as behaviour and never as taste.

context.description: The circumstance around a statement — where, with whom, in what register.

misconception.description: Checked and false: what was believed, what is true, and the source. Written so it is never reasserted.

volatile.description: Mood, venting, hyperbole. Daily notes only; promote on a second occasion or on confirmation.

page-fields.description: The frontmatter every page of this record carries.

entity-body.description: The five-section body: what is known, who it touches, when it happened, what is unsaid, what it used to be.

entity.description: Abstract base for people, animals, organisations, places, ventures, happenings and standing subjects.
entity.use_when: Never directly; author one of its concrete descendants.
entity.avoid_when: Dated capture (daily, review) and pointer records (account, doc, asset).

record.description: Abstract base for the pointer pages: accounts, documents, owned things.
record.use_when: Never directly; author one of its concrete descendants.
record.avoid_when: Anything with its own relationships and narrative (entity).

person.description: One human being who is known, or who matters to the record.
person.use_when: Independent identity, own relationships, and substantial content about one named person.
person.avoid_when: Mentioned in passing (a bullet elsewhere); a group (topic); an animal (pet).

org.description: A company, school, employer, club, or institution.

place.description: A city, neighbourhood, or dwelling that anchors a period of the owner's life.

project.description: A body of work with an aim and a lifecycle.

topic.description: A standing subject — including the domain pages that own facts about the owner.

self.description: The owner's hub: identity and contact channels that have no other home, the life Timeline, and a grouped Relations map. Domain facts live on domain pages.
self.use_when: Exactly one page, and only for what has no domain page to live on.
self.avoid_when: Anything a domain page owns — food, fitness, money, tooling, school.

account.description: A bank, brokerage, or financial-service account.

doc.description: A pointer page for an identity document, permit, visa, or credential.

asset.description: A durable owned thing worth tracking.

daily.description: One day: what happened, what was captured, what is worth a second look.
daily.avoid_when: A fact that will still matter in two weeks; that belongs on a page.

review.description: One ISO week, built from the daily notes and the commit log.

charter.description: The one page that says what this record is for and how facts are ruled in or out.
charter.use_when: Exactly one page — meta/charter.md: what this record remembers and how facts are ruled in or out, loaded every session. Not the agent operating manual (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md).
charter.avoid_when: Anything that is a setting; the constitution is the settings surface.
